item.text: {"case_id":"SHC066","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C09","C20","C19"],"selected_candidate_label":"C09","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C09 is a direct and material drafting template. It concerns the same monument and uses nearly identical recitals about excess Atomic Energy Commission land transferred to the National Park Service with General Services Administration approval. The child repeats C09's operative language for adding and reserving land, extending the monument boundaries, applying monument laws, conditioning activities on the Atomic Energy Commission's noninterference judgment, and warning against damage or settlement. The child adapts that template to a later parcel and adds separate exclusion, restoration, and transfer provisions. C20 is the next strongest because it combines monument enlargement, interagency transfer, monument-law coverage, and a neighboring agency's retained noninterference protection. C19 parallels the add/exclude boundary-revision sequence but lacks the distinctive AEC machinery.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"certain lands of the United States comprising approximately 2882 acres, contiguous to and west of lands of the monument, formerly administered by the Atomic Energy Commission were determined to be in excess of the needs of that agency, and were transferred to the National Park Service ... with the approval of the General Services Administration","parent_excerpt":"certain public lands of the United States comprising approximately 3,600 acres, contiguous to and north of lands set aside for the monument, formerly administered by the Atomic Energy Commission ... were determined to be in excess of the needs of that agency; ... such public lands were transferred to the National Park Service ... with the approval of the General Services Administration","explanation":"Distinctive factual and administrative recital is reused with parcel size, direction, and transfer date changed."},{"child_excerpt":"the following described parcel of land is hereby added to and reserved as a part of the Bandelier National Monument; and the boundaries of such monument are extended accordingly","parent_excerpt":"the following-described lands are hereby added to and reserved as a part of the Bandelier National Monument; and the boundaries of such monument are extended accordingly","explanation":"The central operative formula is virtually verbatim and applies to the same monument."},{"child_excerpt":"Lands hereby added ... shall be subject to all the laws and regulations applicable to such monument and subject to the further restriction that the activities conducted thereon shall be confined to those which in the opinion of the Atomic Energy Commission, will not interfere with the program or operations of the Commission on its adjoining lands.","parent_excerpt":"The lands described above shall be subject to all laws and regulations applicable to the Bandelier National Monument and subject to the further restriction that the activities conducted thereon shall be confined to those which, in the opinion of the Atomic Energy Commission, will not interfere with the program or operations of the Commission in that area.","explanation":"This unusual AEC noninterference restriction is reproduced almost word for word and adapted to adjoining AEC lands."},{"child_excerpt":"Warning is hereby expressly given to all unauthorized persons not to appropriate, injure, destroy, deface or remove any feature of the area herein added to the monument and not to locate or settle upon any of the lands reserved by this proclamation.","parent_excerpt":"Warning is hereby expressly given to all unauthorized persons not to appropriate, injure, destroy, deface, or remove any feature of the area herein added to the monument and not to locate or settle upon any of the lands reserved by this proclamation.","explanation":"The protective warning is essentially verbatim; in combination with the other distinctive overlap, it reinforces direct reuse rather than mere boilerplate similarity."}]}
